audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven level-chart rows disagreed with the packet chart AND with the whys text printed beside them. whys[1] says 'concede this window' while the row read Irelia; whys[2] says 'it stays even' while the row read Irelia; whys[6] says 'He out-scales as a tank' while the row read Irelia.
audit.why: The packet chart (Skill, Nautilus, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Nautilus) matches the prose exactly — the sides were the layer that drifted, not the whys.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 flipped to the packet chart in matched full/content pairs with ratings: 3/10 where Nautilus wins, 5/10 where it is Skill, 7/10 where Irelia wins.

audit.whatIsWrong: First-item spike was named Trinity Force in whys[5] and spikes[2].text while the itemization block on the same page builds Blade of the Ruined King.
audit.why: Internal contradiction; BotRK's %HP and attack speed is what actually spikes the duel against a tank.
audit.corrected: Both renamed to Blade of the Ruined King. Level-6 Vanguard's Edge (125/105/85s) and his Depth Charge (120/100/80s) spikes are otherwise stated correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Irelia's passive with shredding armour/resists in five places (whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid, late, wants.you[2]). Ionian Fervor grants stacking Attack Speed and bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — it does not shred.
audit.why: Riot kit text: 'When Irelia strikes enemies with spells she gains stacking bonus Attack Speed. At maximum stacks she also gains bonus damage on hit.' Against Nautilus this matters directly: the late-game text argued she loses because his resists outpace her shred, when the real reason is that a shred that never existed cannot answer tank stats — %HP damage from Blade of the Ruined King has to.
audit.corrected: All five replaced with max-stack Ionian Fervor attack speed and on-hit damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath was never mentioned as a burst absorber, and dosFull[2] carried unrelated text under a wrong title.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule shield-absorbs-burst; Nautilus W is a flat 12s cooldown at every rank, so it is up for most of your engages unless you force it out.
audit.corrected: Force the shield out before committing — it is 12s flat, not rank-scaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[1].d carried generic boilerplate that did not match their own titles.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range — the single longest punishable window in the lane. Staggering Blow re-arms per target.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your window. With your Bladesurge stacks building and cooldowns tightening, an E-stun into Q-reset out-damages anything he can answer back IF you forced his Q hook out first. Hold W through his E slow-zone (Riptide) and his single-target R knockup — the damage reduction during the channel turns his all-in into your turn to crash resets. At 6, Vanguard's Edge is the key: he is immobile apart from one hook, so dropping the blade wall behind him after he flash-hooks in cuts off his retreat and pins him for the full stacked-passive armor-shred. That is your premier dive.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are your window. With Ionian Fervor stacking and cooldowns tightening, an E-stun into Q-reset out-damages anything he can answer back IF you forced his Q hook out first. Force Titan's Wrath out before you commit — it is 12s flat at every rank and it eats your whole burst, and its auto damage is what W's physical cut actually blunts. At 6, Vanguard's Edge is the key: he is immobile apart from one hook, so dropping the blade wall behind him after he flash-hooks in cuts off his retreat and pins him for the full max-stack on-hit dive. That is your premier window.

edits.before: This lane is genuinely even because he reclaims the late game. As a tank his armor and MR balloon, and while your passive shreds resists once it is stacked, he piles them on faster than you can grind through two items deep. Worse, his entire kit is built to peel you off a carry: Q hook, first-auto root, R knockup — he does not need to kill you, just lock your dash chain out at the wrong moment. Convert your mid-game lead into towers and Heralds before he becomes the unkillable engage bot, because once teamfights start he plays the front-line role he is built for and you do not.
edits.after: This lane is genuinely even because he reclaims the late game. As a tank his armor and MR balloon, and your passive adds attack speed and on-hit damage rather than any shred, so Blade of the Ruined King's %HP is the only thing grinding him down. Worse, his entire kit is built to peel you off a carry: Q hook, first-auto root, R knockup — he does not need to kill you, just lock your dash chain out at the wrong moment. Convert your mid-game lead into towers and Heralds before he becomes the unkillable engage bot, because once teamfights start he plays the front-line role he is built for and you do not.

notes: Two systemic problems here. (1) The level chart disagreed with its own whys text on six rows; the packet chart matched the prose, so the sides were corrected to it in matched pairs. (2) The same 'passive armour shred' fiction found on the nasus entry appears five times here, and it is load-bearing — the late-game paragraph explains Irelia's fall-off as 'he stacks resists faster than you shred', which is a wrong causal story. Titan's Wrath's flat 12s cooldown is now stated. UNVERIFIED and left alone: the early paragraph claims a root landing mid-dash cancels Bladesurge; Riot's text does not state dash-cancel behaviour and the kit file's needsResearch is empty by design, so I did not assert or deny it.
